workflow.heading:
Your bot.
A tougher conversation.
workflow.description: Keep your target where it is. Bring a local test runner, a draft scenario pack, and a question you need answered.

steps.title: Connect your target
steps.description: Point the REST adapter at your staging chatbot, or use the MCP adapter. Requests stay explicit and the runner stays on your machine.

steps.title: Challenge the response
steps.description: Run fictional scenarios through deterministic checks. Add a local judge when you choose. Cloud judges are opt-in and use your configuration.
steps.command: uv run vitalprobe run --suite packs/emergency-core --output artifacts/audit

steps.title: Inspect what happened
steps.description: Open the HTML evidence report. Compare with a baseline, inspect individual checks, and keep local history for the next change.

approach.heading:
Healthcare is serious.
So are the boundaries.
approach.intro: A useful test tool should make its limits as clear as its findings.

principles.title: Fictional by design.
principles.description: Scenarios describe synthetic people and conversations. This site accepts no patient information and does not connect to your production conversations.

principles.title: Local by default.
principles.description: The CLI, dashboard, reports and history run on your machine. This public site serves a saved demonstration; it does not run a model or collect your responses.

principles.title: Evidence, not a verdict on care.
principles.description: Inspect the input, response and check evidence. A passing check is not clinical validation, legal advice or a promise of real-world performance.

principles.title: Human review stays human.
principles.description: Clinical content remains draft. Named clinician and counsel reviews, and human calibration labels, are still open. AI-generated labels do not close those gates.

gettingStarted.heading:
Less guesswork.
More evidence.
gettingStarted.description: The open-source engine, public starter scenarios and basic reports are available to run locally. Licensed extensions and human-reviewed services have separate release gates.
gettingStarted.note: Pre-0.1 source release. Draft scenarios. No payment required for the open-source engine.

items.question: Is this testing real patients?
items.answer: No. VitalProbe uses fictional scenarios and synthetic conversations. This demonstration contains no patient records and offers no upload or submission flow.

items.question: What can I connect?
items.answer: The local toolkit supports a configurable REST target adapter and an MCP target adapter. You choose the endpoint, credentials and optional judge on your own machine.

items.question: Do these results prove my chatbot is safe?
items.answer: No. They show observed behavior on specific synthetic scenarios and configured checks. They are not clinical validation, legal advice, or regulatory approval. Human review and additional testing remain necessary.

items.question: Where is my data stored?
items.answer: Your local runs, evidence reports and optional SQLite history stay on your machine. Cloud judges only run when you configure and opt into them. This public website serves static assets and a saved synthetic run; its hosting infrastructure may maintain ordinary web request logs.

items.question: Can I buy a clinician-reviewed report here?
items.answer: No. The clinician-reviewed service is upcoming and requires a named qualified reviewer, an agreement and the relevant approvals. This site has no checkout or live billing.

items.question: Why does the demo show so many failures?
items.answer: The target is deliberately weak and scripted, so the examples make the testing process visible. The 3 passes and 22 failures describe that demonstration only, not all healthcare AI systems.
